hunks.sol: “…You might as well ask for his last words. At this point, it sounds like you just want him dead.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang frowned at my quiet rebuttal.

hunks.baseline: “You’re too soft. Sometimes you have to do this to squeeze even one more word out of someone.”
hunks.sol: “You’re too soft. Sometimes you have to squeeze a man to get even one more word out of him.”

hunks.sol: Ten years was easy to say. But he’d had to recall, in detail and without a wink of sleep, everything that had happened over a span long enough for mountains and rivers to change. No wonder he’d turned into a half-dried squid in just over a day.

hunks.baseline: “P-please believe me. I really did tell you everything. I didn’t leave out a single thing.”

hunks.baseline: The stories kept piling up, one after another, like sweet potato vines that kept coming no matter how many you pulled.
hunks.sol: The absurd stories kept coming, like sweet potato vines that refused to end no matter how many you pulled up. Listening to them, I couldn’t help wondering:

hunks.baseline: They were so absurd that, as I listened, I couldn’t help thinking:
Everyone had their own ambitions.
hunks.sol: Everyone wanted something.

hunks.baseline: Regardless of whether they were good or bad, there was bound to be some goal a person had carried in their heart at least once.
hunks.sol: Right or wrong, everyone had some goal they’d held in their heart at least once.

hunks.baseline: But the Lord in their stories fit none of them.
hunks.sol: But Great Sir, as they described him, fit none of the possibilities.

hunks.baseline: He hadn’t taken over Ningxia and ruled as a mighty conqueror. Nor was he a notorious fiend who’d slipped into the frontier to hide his identity, or a hermit master wandering where no one would find him because he was nearing the end of his life.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t taken over Ningxia and ruled it as a mighty conqueror. Nor did he sound like a notorious fiend hiding his identity on the frontier, or a hermit master wandering where no one would find him as his life drew to a close.

hunks.baseline: *If he wanted to rule as a conqueror, there’d be no reason to hole up in a cave. If he were a fiend, he’d have tried his damnedest to keep his identity hidden—or from the start, he’d have put the mounted bandits under his command.*
hunks.sol: *If he wanted to rule, why hole up in a cave? If he were a fiend, he’d be desperate to keep his identity hidden before anyone recognized him. Or he’d have taken the mounted bandits as his followers from the start.*

hunks.baseline: If he were a hermit master, there wasn’t even much to think about.
hunks.sol: As for a hermit master, I hardly needed to think about it.

hunks.baseline: Honestly, what kind of deranged hermit would choose the frontier, with its year-round high levels of fine dust and blowing yellow sand, over some remote mountain valley with beautiful scenery and clear water?
hunks.sol: What kind of deranged hermit would pass up a remote mountain valley with beautiful scenery and clear water to settle on a frontier where fine dust hung in the air and yellow sand blew through all year?

hunks.baseline: Even I knew the famous poet Paul Valéry. If he’d lived in Ningxia Province instead of France, he would’ve written, *The yellow dust is blowing. Fuck, I want to die.*
hunks.sol: Even an ignoramus like me knew the famous poet Paul Valéry. If he’d lived in Ningxia Province instead of France, he would’ve written, *The yellow dust is blowing. Fuck, I want to die.*

hunks.baseline: *And it wasn’t as if he were an old man gone senile, or a dying elder who didn’t need to seek out some remote mountain valley, either.*
hunks.sol: *And it wasn’t as if he were some senile old man, or someone so close to death that finding a mountain valley wasn’t worth the trouble.*
